source.title: Open questions for operators related to rectangular Catalan combinatorics

accepted.question_text: Let Theta_{a,b} be the elliptic Hall algebra construction that sends a degree-d symmetric-function seed g_d to an operator, and write g_d^(a,b)(x;q,t) for Theta_{a,b}(g_d)(1). Let s_hat_mu be the normalized Schur seed defined by s_hat_mu(x) = (-qt)^(-iota(mu)) s_mu(x), where mu is a partition of d and iota(mu) is the statistic defined from the positive values of mu(i)-i. For every partition mu of d and every coprime pair of positive integers a and b, prove that s_hat_mu^(a,b)(x;q,t) is Schur-positive, meaning that its expansion in the Schur basis has coefficients in N[q,t]. Can this Schur positivity be explained by bigraded subrepresentations of the S_n-module of generalized diagonal harmonics?
accepted.context_brief: Schur positivity for normalized Schur seeds

accepted.question_text: Let Theta_{a,b} and g_d^(a,b)(x;q,t) be as above. For a partition mu of d, let m_hat_mu(x) = (-1)^(d-length(mu)) m_mu(x) be the normalized monomial symmetric-function seed and let f_hat_mu(x) = (-qt)^(-(length(mu)-1)) f_mu(x) be the normalized forgotten symmetric-function seed. For every partition mu of d and every coprime pair of positive integers a and b, prove that both m_hat_mu^(a,b)(x;q,t) and f_hat_mu^(a,b)(x;q,t) are Schur-positive. Can these Schur-positive expressions be realized as bigraded Frobenius characteristics of suitable bigraded S_n-modules?
accepted.context_brief: Schur positivity for normalized monomial and forgotten seeds

accepted.question_text: For coprime positive integers a and b, consecutive hook shapes (j+1|k-1) and (j|k), and the normalized Schur-seed functions s_hat_(j+1|k-1)^(a,b)(x;q,t) and s_hat_(j|k)^(a,b)(x;q,t), prove the Schur inclusion q s_hat_(j+1|k-1)^(a,b)(x;q,t) <=_s s_hat_(j|k)^(a,b)(x;q,t), where <=_s means that the difference is Schur-positive. Also, for all positive integers m and n, prove the Schur inclusion q^beta e_{m-1,n}(x;q,t) <=_s h_hat_{m,n}(x;q,t), where beta is the number of points between the diagonal-avoiding (m,n)-staircase path and the (m-1,n)-staircase path as defined in the source.

accepted.question_text: Let the bar operator on symmetric functions be defined by sending s_mu(x) to s_mu_bar(x), where mu_bar is obtained from the partition mu by removing its first column, and extending linearly. For all positive integers m and n, prove the transpose Schur inclusions q^alpha' bar(e_{m,n-1}(x;q,t)) <=_s e_{m,n}(x;q,t) and q^beta' bar(e_{m,n-1}(x;q,t)) <=_s h_hat_{m,n}(x;q,t), where alpha' and beta' are the staircase-counting exponents described for the transpose versions of the inclusions.

accepted.question_text: For any good seed g_d, meaning a seed whose associated functions g_d^(a,b)(x;q,t) are Schur-positive, and for every coprime pair of positive integers b >= a, prove the transpose Schur inclusion bar(g_d^(b,a)(x;q,t)) <=_s g_d^(a,b)(x;q,t). The bar operator is needed because g_d^(b,a) and g_d^(a,b) have different symmetric-function degrees.

accepted.question_text: For m >= n, prove that every LLT-polynomial gamma_{m,n}(x;t) associated to an (m,n)-Dyck path has an elementary-basis expansion with coefficients in N[r] after the specialization t=1+r, i.e. 0 <=_e gamma_{m,n}(x;1+r). This would help explain both Schur positivity of g_d^(a,b)(x;q,t) and e-positivity of g_d^(a,b)(x;q,1+r) when such functions expand positively in these LLT-polynomials.

evidence.quote: we have experimentally observed that these LLT-polynomials expand positively in the elementary function basis when spe-cialized at t = 1 + r
